submission.natural_language_explanation: This head copies a scope operator forward: at the first word or two of a negated, restricted or quantified phrase it attends sharply back (weight 0.7-0.95) to the operator that opened the phrase - a negator ('not', "n't", 'never', 'no', 'nothing', 'nobody', 'hardly', 'rarely', 'without'), a restrictive/focus particle ('only', 'just', 'merely', 'even', 'also', 'still') or a frequency/quantifier adverb ('always', 'often', 'usually', 'all') - and writes that operator's direction into the current token, making its write far from its mean. Prompts are therefore active on the token(s) right after such an operator ('not very', 'only two', 'never easy', 'all afternoon') and stay near the mean in affirmative prose and after plain degree adverbs ('very', 'so', 'quite', 'extremely'); in code the string-argument opener '("' or an opening quote plays the same operator role (largest writes at format specifiers such as %s/%v and escapes such as \n), and a text's second token is weakly active when the text opens with a pronoun subject, since the head copies the unmeasured first-token sink.

rival_explanations: A narrower reading: the head is a pure negation detector ('not', "n't", 'never', 'no'), so restrictive or focus particles such as 'only' and 'just' leave it below the activity line and belong to a different function.
A broader reading: the head fires after any adverb it attends to, degree adverbs included, so 'It was very clear to us' and 'quite easy' should also cross the activity line.
